label: Early copy phase (2nd/3rd output) of long sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, right after <DEL>: mainly on the step that receives original token 0 as input and outputs original token 1 (recall_idx 1; 85% of activation mass), and more weakly one step later (recall_idx 2; 15%). Strength rises steeply with sequence length: it is rare for L <= 6, frequent at L = 7, and strongest at L = 8-9 (L=9 holds 55% of mass). The top activations are all recall_idx 1 with L = 9, and the second-step activation is usually much weaker than the first. Never fires during the original phase, on the <DEL> step, at recall_idx 0, or from recall_idx 3 on (apart from a trace near the end of L=9 sequences). Token identity has only a mild effect (inputs o, l, x are somewhat higher). Main errors: false positives at recall_idx 2 when L = 8-9, where it fires inconsistently, and weak misses at recall_idx 1 for L = 5-6.

issues: The claim that token identity matters only a little is false. The per-L marginal hides it. Within each borderline cell, the identity of the input token (orig(0) at recall_idx 1, orig(1) at recall_idx 2) moves firing precision across nearly its whole range. At recall_idx 2, L=9 it ranges from 0.04 (s), 0.07 (q) and 0.11 (y) up to 0.995 (l), 0.996 (o) and 0.98 (x). At recall_idx 1, L=7 it ranges from 0.04 (y) and 0.10 (s) up to 1.0 (l, o, x). The ranking stays the same across cells. High tokens: c, h, i, l, n, o, v, x, digit 2. Low tokens: a, b, f, p, q, s, t, u, y.

The false positives are not 'inconsistent firing'. They are a systematic class: recall_idx 2, L=9 steps where the input orig(1) is a low token (u, w, b, y, ...). The rendered test false positives show this, for example *u*, *w*, *b*, *y* after <DEL>.

The missed activations at recall_idx 1, L=6 (precision 0.21 overall) and recall_idx 2, L=8 (0.31) are also token-gated. For example, l/o/x at L=6 reach 0.68-0.94 and l/o/x at L=8 reach 0.81-0.90. They are not weak noise.

Minor: the explanation lists recall_idx 2 with L=8-9 as false positives, but the predicate only includes L=9 for recall_idx 2, so L=8 at recall_idx 2 is actually a miss class. The positional, phase and L-mass claims do check out: no firing in the original phase, on <DEL>, or at recall_idx 0; recall_idx 1 holds 85% of the mass and L=9 holds 55%.
